<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="" />{{rh|CHA. X.|ACCORDING TO S. MARKE.|115}}</noinclude>{{verse|chapter=10|verse=35}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 20, 20.''}}* there come to him Iames and Iohn the sonnes of Zebedee, saying, Maister, vve vvil that vvhat thing soeuer vve shal aske, thou doe it to vs. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=36}}† But he said to them, What vvil you that I doe to you? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=37}}† And they said, Graunt to vs, that vve may sit, one on thy right hand, and the other on thy left hand, in thy glorie. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=38}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to them, You vvotte not vvhat you aske. can you drinke the cuppe that I drinke: or be baptized vvith the baptisme vvhervvith I am baptized? {{verse|chapter=10|verse=39}}† But they said to him, VVe can. And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to them, The cuppe in deede vvhich I drinke, you shal drinke: and vvith the baptisme vvhervvith I am baptized, shal you be baptized: {{verse|chapter=10|verse=40}}† but to sit on my right hand or on my left, is not mine to giue vnto you, but to vvhom it is prepared. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=41}}† And the ten hearing, began to be displeased at Iames and Iohn. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=42}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} calling them, saith to them, {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 20, 25. Lu. 22, 25.''}}* You knovv that they vvhich seeme to rule ouer the gentiles, ouerrule them: and their Princes haue povver ouer them. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=43}}† But it is not so in you. but vvhosoeuer vvil be greater, shal be your minister: {{verse|chapter=10|verse=44}}† and vvhosoeuer vvil be first among you, shal be the seruant of al. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=45}}† For the Sonne of man also is not come to be ministred vnto, but to minister, and to giue his life a redempption for many. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=46}}† And {{MarginNote|margin=left|margin-width=65|text=''Mt. 20, 29. Lu. 18, 35.''}}* they come to Iericho: and vvhen he departed from Iericho, and his Disciples, and a very great multitude, the sonne of Timæus, Bar-timæus the blinde man, sate by the way side begging. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=47}}† VVho vvhen he had heard, that it is {{sc|Iesvs}} of Nazareth: he began to crie, and to say, {{sc|Iesvs}}, sonne of Dauid, haue mercie vpon me. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=48}}† And many threatened him, to hold his peace. but he cried much more, Sonne of Dauid, {{verse|chapter=10|verse=49}}† haue mercie vpon me. And {{sc|Iesvs}} standing stil commaunded him to be called. And they call the blinde man, saying to him, Be of better comfort, arise, he calleth thee. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=50}}† VVho casting of his garment leapt vp, and came to him. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=51}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} ansvvering, said to him, VVhat vvilt thou that I doe vnto thee? And the blinde man said to him, Rabbôni, that I may see. {{verse|chapter=10|verse=52}}† And {{sc|Iesvs}} said to him, Goe thy vvaies, thy faith hath made the safe. And forthvvith he savv, and folovved him in the vvay.<noinclude>{{rh||P ij|ANNOT}}</noinclude>
